Model Implied Covariance Matrix of a One-Factor Confirmatory Factor Model

Source: R/covmat_from_cfa.R
covmat_from_cfa.Rd

Computes the covariance matrix of the indicators that a single-factor confirmatory factor model implies, from the factor loadings and the residual variances of the indicators: $$\Sigma = \lambda \lambda^\top + \Theta, \qquad \Theta = \mathrm{diag}(\theta_1, \ldots, \theta_p).$$ The loadings and residual variances may be population values, for a covariance matrix to plan a study or to simulate from, or estimates from a fitted model, for the covariance matrix the fitted model implies. The calculation is the same in both cases, and the result is the model implied covariance matrix: the population covariance matrix of the model when the inputs are population values, and the fitted model's covariance matrix when they are estimates.

Usage

covmat_from_cfa(factor_loading, residual_var, tol_det = 1e-05)

Arguments

factor_loading

A numeric vector of factor loadings, one per indicator (at least two), on the metric of a factor with variance 1. A single-row or single-column matrix is accepted and read as a vector. Population loadings or estimates from a fitted model.

residual_var

A numeric vector of residual variances (unique or error variances), one per indicator, or a single value used for every indicator (the equal residual variance model). Population values or estimates from a fitted model.

tol_det

The value below which the determinant of the implied covariance matrix triggers a warning that the matrix may not be positive definite (default 1e-05).

Value

A list with the single element model_implied_cov: the model implied covariance matrix of the indicators, a symmetric \(p \times p\) matrix.

Details

Under the single-factor model, each indicator score is \(x_i = \lambda_i \xi + \delta_i\), where \(\xi\) is the common factor and \(\delta_i\) is the residual of indicator i, with variance \(\theta_i\), uncorrelated with the factor and with the other residuals. The general form of the model implied covariance matrix, \(\Lambda \Phi \Lambda^\top + \Theta\), reduces to \(\lambda \lambda^\top + \Theta\) here: \(\Lambda\) is the \(p \times 1\) column of loadings \(\lambda = (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_p)^\top\) (factor_loading), the factor variance \(\Phi\) is fixed at 1, and \(\Theta\) is the diagonal matrix of the residual variances (residual_var). Because \(\Theta\) is diagonal, the residuals are uncorrelated by construction; a model with correlated residuals needs a more general formulation than this function provides.

Estimates from a fit that fixed one loading at 1 and estimated the factor variance \(\phi\) are put on this metric by multiplying each loading by \(\sqrt{\phi}\); the residual variances are unchanged, and so is the implied matrix. cfa_1 fixes the factor variance at 1, so its loadings and residual variances can be given as they are.

Estimated residual variances at or below 0 (a Heywood case) are used as given; the function does not check their sign. The determinant check warns only when the determinant of the implied matrix is below tol_det, which a Heywood case need not produce: with loadings .9, .8, and 1.1 and residual variances .2, .3, and -.01, the implied matrix is positive definite and no warning is given. A determinant above tol_det does not show that the matrix is positive definite either, because an even number of negative eigenvalues gives a positive determinant. Check the residual variances themselves for a Heywood case, and the eigenvalues of the result for positive definiteness.

The cfa spelling matches the cfa_1 naming.

See also

cfa_1, ss_aipe_reliability

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# Five indicators with equal loadings and equal residual variances
covmat_from_cfa(factor_loading = rep(0.7, 5), residual_var = rep(0.51, 5))
#> $model_implied_cov
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5]
#> [1,] 1.00 0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49
#> [2,] 0.49 1.00 0.49 0.49 0.49
#> [3,] 0.49 0.49 1.00 0.49 0.49
#> [4,] 0.49 0.49 0.49 1.00 0.49
#> [5,] 0.49 0.49 0.49 0.49 1.00
#> 

# Unequal loadings
covmat_from_cfa(factor_loading = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8),
                residual_var   = c(0.75, 0.64, 0.51, 0.36))
#> $model_implied_cov
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,] 1.00 0.30 0.35 0.40
#> [2,] 0.30 1.00 0.42 0.48
#> [3,] 0.35 0.42 1.00 0.56
#> [4,] 0.40 0.48 0.56 1.00
#> 

# From the estimates of a fitted one-factor model, whose factor variance
# cfa_1() fixes at 1: the covariance matrix the fitted model implies for
# four verbal tests of holzinger_swineford. The tests have no missing
# scores, so the model is fit to their covariance matrix, which gives
# the estimates the raw scores give.
items <- c("t5_general_information", "t6_paragraph_comprehension",
           "t7_sentence", "t9_word_meaning")
fit <- cfa_1(S = cov(holzinger_swineford[, items]), N = 301)
covmat_from_cfa(
  factor_loading = fit$estimate[grepl("=~", fit$syntax)],
  residual_var = fit$estimate[fit$syntax %in% paste(items, "~~", items)])
#> $model_implied_cov
#>           [,1]     [,2]     [,3]     [,4]
#> [1,] 152.77322 29.55780 45.69592 67.70201
#> [2,]  29.55780 12.15598 12.72080 18.84684
#> [3,]  45.69592 12.72080 26.55657 29.13693
#> [4,]  67.70201 18.84684 29.13693 58.62156
#>
